intro: Aunque can mean although or even if. Mood and context show how the speaker frames the concession.
p.a pesar de que: in spite of the fact that
p.sino.nota: After a negative, sino replaces or corrects an element: no es rojo, sino azul. With a following conjugated clause, use sino que.
p.y eso que: and even though (colloquial; introduces a surprising fact)
p.llover.nota: Llueva is the present subjunctive used for a possible condition.
p.mojarse.nota: Nos mojamos is the past form: we got wet.
b1.texto:
**Aunque** can introduce a factual or a possible concession; mood and context show how the speaker frames it. It does not map one-to-one onto “although” versus “even if.”

- **Aunque está lloviendo**, salgo. (I present the rain as a current fact.)
- **Aunque llueva**, saldré. (I'll go regardless of whether it rains.)
- —Es muy caro. —**Aunque sea** caro, lo quiero. (The price is already part of the conversation.)

**A pesar de** takes a noun or infinitive: **a pesar del frío**, **a pesar de** estar cansado. **A pesar de que** takes a clause, and its mood also depends on how the concession is framed: **a pesar de que haga frío**, iremos.

**Sin embargo**, **aun así**, and **de todas formas** contrast with what came before; punctuation often sets them apart.

**Pero** marks a contrast. After a negative, **sino** corrects or replaces an element: no es español, **sino** mexicano. With a following conjugated clause, use **sino que**: no estudia, **sino que** trabaja.

**Y eso que** is colloquial and introduces a surprising fact: suspendí, **y eso que** estudié mucho.
b2.f0: Tomorrow we're going on the outing, even if it rains.
b2.f1: Although I'm tired, I'm coming with you.
b2.f2: In spite of the cold, it's going to be fun.
b2.f3: I'm not taking an umbrella, but a coat.
b2.f4: Last year we got wet. Even so, we had a good time.
b4.pregunta: Complete: even if it rains tomorrow, I'll go.
b4.o0.refuerzo: This frames the rain as a possible condition, not as a stated fact.
b4.o1.refuerzo: The indicative would state it as a fact.
b4.o2.refuerzo: Aunque does not take the future here.
b5.pregunta: Use the indicative to present this as a new fact: although I'm tired, I'm going.
b5.o0.refuerzo: The speaker presents tiredness as an asserted fact here.
b5.o1.refuerzo: The subjunctive can frame a concession as background or hypothetical; this prompt asks for a new asserted fact.
b6.pregunta: Complete: it isn't red, but blue.
b6.o1.refuerzo: After a negative that is corrected, Spanish uses sino.
b7.pregunta: Complete: in spite of the rain.
b7.o0.refuerzo: A pesar de plus a noun.
b7.o1.refuerzo: A pesar de que needs a clause.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The phrase is a pesar de.
b8.traduccion: Even so, we had a very good time.
b9.pregunta: Complete the correction: he doesn't study; rather, he works.
b9.o0.refuerzo: Use sino que before a conjugated clause that replaces the negative statement.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Sino alone is used before a noun, adjective, or infinitive.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Pero contrasts ideas without correcting the first one.
b10.pregunta: Complete: in spite of the fact that it is cold, we'll go.
b10.o0.refuerzo: A pesar de que introduces a full clause.
b10.o1.refuerzo: A pesar de can precede a noun or infinitive, not this finite clause.
b10.o2.refuerzo: The standard expression includes de before que.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about things you do in spite of the difficulties, and things you will do whatever happens.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Defend aloud a plan that everybody criticises: Aunque sea caro…, a pesar de que…
